hits.title: Lumière ! par Thierry Frémaux
hits.content: 130 years ago, Louis and Auguste Lumière invented the Cinématographe and the movie theatre. Everything was already there: framing, tracking shots, drama, comedy and acting. By filming Lyon, Paris and the entire planet, they brought the world to the world. | Drawing on a selection of one hundred beautifully restored Lumière films, Thierry Frémaux, General Delegate of the Cannes Film Festival and Managing Director of the Institut Lumière in Lyon, explores the legacy of the Lumière brothers while providing live commentary on these unforgettable images, restored to their original splendour. An extraordinary cinematic and historical experience, presented in Montreal as a special event during Festival CINEMANIA’s 32nd edition. | ["1h30","Original French Version","General Admission"] | ["Production \/ Presentation: Festival CINEMANIA"]

hits.title: Labrador, Autopsie du silence par Rodrigue Jean
hits.content: Off the coast of Labrador, a storm strikes a merchant ship carrying supplies to Inuit communities in the Far North. As the tempest rages outside, a violent incident erupts in the heart of the vessel and shakes the crew. | The name of Alupa, a young Inuit mechanic, surfaces as the ensuing investigation unfolds. His fate suddenly takes a turn, taking with it the unique bond he shares with his best friend on board. hits.title: Le fantôme dans la machine
hits.content: Invited onto a television set, Rousse gets the surprise of her life: the production team has organized a live reunion with her brother, whom she hasn’t seen in 29 years. Except he died in a fire in 1997. | Is it a hallucination? A tasteless prank? An attempt at making “good TV”? And that’s only the beginning: her brother reappears in other unlikely places, asking what became of Lady Di, whether anyone ever patched the hole in the ozone layer… Unfinished conversations and bickering pick up almost as if nothing had changed. Soon, in this atmosphere both strange and familiar, every possible version of her brother comes to haunt and roast her, toying with her certainties. Rousse finds herself engaged in introspection in spite of herself: imagining her brother’s lives means rethinking her own. And you, what would you say if your own ghosts came to chat?Fanny Britt (Bienveillance, Hurlevents, Classique(s)) has written a clever, playful and touching text, directed by Alexia Bürger (Les Hardings, Les filles du Saint Laurent, Camera obscura), her friend and collaborator since childhood, with all the understated simplicity that is her signature. On stage, a revolving platform whose trapdoors open at the whim of the brothers’ moods, a bit like planets aligning to influence us (or so some believe!), or like a wheel of fate that at times seems about to go haywire. Both autobiographical and pure invention, this show nests its stories within one another like Russian dolls. A deeply moving tribute to all those who are no longer quite here, but who made us who we are… or who we might have been. | ["French","November 12, 2026","November 13, 2026"] | ["Text: Fanny Britt","Stage Direction: Alexia Bürger","Interpretation: Anne-Élisabeth Bossé, Patrice Dubois, Simon Lacroix, Christophe Levac","Dramaturgy: Chloé Gagné Dion","Staging Assistance: Stéphanie Capistran-Lalonde","Scenography and Lighting Design: Martin Labrecque","Costumes: Elen Ewing","Music: Philippe Brault","Props: Julie Measroch","Makeup and hairstyling: Justine Denoncourt-Bélanger","Movement: Jamie Wright","Video: Béatrice Germain","Production \/ Presentation: Duceppe","Collaboration: Place des Arts"]

hits.title: Entre chiens et louves
hits.content: Pianist and composer Alexandra Stréliski accompanies the artists of Cirque Le Roux on stage for this dazzling show, featuring a musical score of her own works and other equally captivating pieces. Presented exclusively at Place des Arts, this unique version of Entre chiens et louves promises to be a memorable experience.  | Entre chiens et louves (Between Dogs and Wolves) immerses the audience in a historical epic that reveals the intimacy of three characters living in different eras: 1850, 1960, and 2026. Tracing their journeys, the piece is a staggering excursion through time, taking us right up to the present day, evoking the collective memories that make us who we are—filled with revolt and emancipation—but which still divide us today. A true testament to the human condition, the piece depicts a world full of hope, of bodies in motion, offering a glimpse of the forgotten who are just waiting to be reborn. Conceived much like a film in which the scenes unfold, the piece gives free rein to eight virtuosos who draw us into an epic adventure blending comedy, spectacular acrobatics, and dance with an impetus that is profoundly human and supportive. Accompanied by string duo Julia and Natalia Kotarba and electronic musician Jimbo Canoville, Alexandra Stréliski will perform four of her own compositions — two from Néo-Romance and two created for Entre chiens et louves — along with classics by Schubert, Chopin, Pergolesi, Vivaldi, Beethoven and Nina Simone. A Montreal premiere that will bring a new dimension to this critically acclaimed production, which has been performed more than 250 times across Europe.Cirque Le Roux Founded in France in 2014, Cirque Le Roux is renowned for its originality, refined aesthetics, narrative power, and exceptional technical virtuosity. Always seeking to innovate, this contemporary circus company brings together artists from various countries and diverse backgrounds, many of whom studied at the National Circus School in Montreal, where they met Alexandra Stréliski. By blending acrobatics, theatre, and humour, Cirque Le Roux creates unique shows that redefine the conventions of the modern circus.  | ["1h20 without intermission","Press Premiere"] | ["Artistic, Visual, and Acrobatic Direction: Cirque Le Roux  ","Stage Direction: Cirque Le Roux, Charlotte Saliou","Choreography: Maria Carolina Vieira","Text: Léonard Kahn","Scenography: Cirque Le Roux, Benoît Probst","Costumes: Cirque Le Roux, Clarisse Baudinière","Lighting Design: Pierre Berneron","Sound: Jimbo Canoville","Music: Alexandra Stréliski ","Production Management: Juliette Grandmottet","Assistant Stage Director: Nina Quitté","Interpretation: Philip Rosenberg, Kaisha Dessalines-Wright, Mathilde Jimenez, Tristan Nielsen, Maude Parent, Greg Arsenal, Yannick Thomas, Samuel Charlton","On-Stage Musical Performers: Alexandra Stréliski, Julia Kotarba, Natalia Kotarba, Jimbo Canoville ","Diffusion: Place des Arts","Co-production: Le Bon Marché Rive Gauche, Cirque Le Roux","Collaboration: La Presse","Support: Consulat général de France à Québec","Media partner: Radio-Canada"]

hits.title: The Thousand and One Notes of Sheherazade
hits.artist: Orchestre symphonique de Montréal, Alexandre Tharaud, Dina Gilbert
hits.content: Past and present converse in this journey through the sounds and imaginings of the Orient.  | With Scheherazade, Rimsky-Korsakov unfolds the legend of the storyteller whose strength, finesse, and ingenuity triumph over fear: Andrew Wan’s violin embodies her deep, supple, sovereign voice, while conductor Dina Gilbert leads the orchestra like the heroine weaving her destiny. In counterpoint, French composer Thierry Pécou draw us “in the manner of Bali” into his Cara Bali Concerto, performed by pianist Alexandre Tharaud, the work’s dedicatee. Inspired by the cycles, timbres, and poetry of the gamelan, this concerto becomes a bridge to a vibrant elsewhere, where imaginary percussion and piano intertwine in a ballet of interlaced energies. A sensory crossing between legend, rhythm, and light.This concert is also presented with a condensed program. | ["1h45 with intermission (November 11) | 1h without intermission (November 12)"] | [": Thierry Pécou, Cara Bali Concerto (43 min)_Nikolai Rimsky-Korsakov, Sheherazade, op. 35 (42 min)","Conductor: Dina Gilbert","Piano: Alexandre Tharaud","Production \/ Presentation: Orchestre symphonique de Montréal (OSM)","Presentation: Fondation J.A. hits.title: Ni vue, Ni connue par Marc Fitoussi
hits.content: Corinne Maclou (Isabelle Huppert) has always been a film extra. From one shoot to the next, she dreams of landing the role that will finally bring her out of the shadows. | Her encounter with actress Sandrine Kiberlain, who plays herself, seems to open the door to new opportunities. But will their budding friendship withstand Corinne's expectations? In this comedy about dreams of fame and power dynamics, Sandrine Kiberlain’s effortless and acute acting instincts shine opposite an irresistible Isabelle Huppert. With Ni vue, Ni connue (All About Corinne), Marc Fitoussi returns to Festival CINEMANIA for the first time since 2010, when he presented Copacabana, also starring Isabelle Huppert.Selected at Toronto International Film Festival (TIFF) and Locarno Film Festival, this film will be presented as a Quebec premiere at this 32nd edition of Festival CINEMANIA. | ["1h55","Original French version, subtitled in English","General admission"] | ["Direction: Marc Fitoussi","Cast: Isabelle Huppert, Sandrine Kiberlain","Production \/ Presentation: Festival CINEMANIA"]

Then comes Scheherazade, where the violin—Andrew Wan’s voice—traces the destiny of the heroine from One Thousand and One Nights. Its supple, mesmerizing lines sketch her strategies, doubts, gentleness, and audacity as she gradually tames the sultan and turns her story into salvation. hits.title: Les rayons et les ombres par Xavier Giannoli
hits.content: Around 1930, French journalist Jean Luchaire and German Otto Abetz work toward bringing their two countries closer together. | But war breaks out: Abetz becomes the Reich's ambassador to Paris, and their prewar friendship gradually gives way to collaboration. Under his protection, Luchaire becomes a powerful press magnate and drags down with him his daughter Corinne, a young actress destined for a brilliant career. After Lost Illusions, Xavier Giannoli delivers a sweeping historical epic about the spiral of compromise, blindness and fascination with power. hits.content: In three hours, Nina will reveal her directorial debut at the Comédie-Française. hits.content: Welcome to the 6th edition of Micro ouvert autochtone (Indigenous Open Mic), a grand celebration of Indigenous cultures. hits.title: Heroines and Lyrical Passions
hits.artist: Orchestre Métropolitain, Keri-Lynn Wilson, Sarah Dufresne
hits.content:
Some figures endure through the centuries, inspiring the greatest artists. Manon Lescaut, the heroine of the Abbé Prévost novel, embodies tragic passion: smitten and seductive, yet doomed to a cruel fate. | 
    Soprano Sarah Dufresne brings this legendary figure to life by combining arias from two famous adaptations, by Auber and Massenet, to map out her psychological journey.


    Alongside Manon, Keri-Lynn Wilson leads the OM in orchestral works by Clémence de Grandval, a pioneering female composer who carved a place for herself in a predominantly male world. Tchaikovsky and Wagner’s symphonic masterpieces then carry us through the tragic passions of Francesca da Rimini, heroine of The Divine Comedy, and Isolde, Tristan’s mythical lover.

venues: Piano Nobile de la Salle Wilfrid-Pelletier
hits.content: Mokatek in Reading: A meeting of words, music, and song that brings a story to life, celebrating the power of Indigenous imagination, the passing down of knowledge, and the bonds that connect us to our roots. | Let yourself be swept away by a storybook reading about little Mokatek, who loves counting the stars as he drifts off to sleep. hits.content: The Duplex, the hilarious comedy that triumphed in Paris, is coming to Quebec for the very first time! This play by Didier Caron, featuring the excellent actors Pascale Desrochers, Sylvain Marcel, Valérie Blais, and François Massicotte, promises a healthy dose of madness, bursts of laughter… and neighbours who didn't see it coming! | Meet the Bergerons, who live on the top floor of an apartment building. They feel so at home there that they dream of expanding their nest by taking over the apartment of the Tessiers, their charming friends and downstairs neighbours, in order to create a two-story residence. But the Tessiers are happy in their own place and have no intention of packing their bags. The Bergerons will have to use every trick in the book to achieve their goal and finally get their neighbours to leave. What follows is a series of twisted schemes, dubious machinations, and hilarious misunderstandings that will severely test their friendship… and their shared walls!The Duplex: Evicting your neighbours has never been so funny! | ["French"] | ["Text: Didier Caron","Interpretation: Pascale Desrochers, Sylvain Marcel, Valérie Blais, François Massicotte","Production \/ Presentation: Fun Nation"]

hits.title: Werther | Jules Massenet
hits.content: Coproduced with the Canadian Opera Company and Vancouver Opera, Werther features an exceptional cast, marking the grand return of Julie Boulianne to the Opéra de Montréal and the Montreal debut of the rising French tenor Julien Dran. | The production, true to late 18th-century Germany, is built around a central set piece: an engraving of the town of Wetzlar, where the story unfolds. It is the perfect showcase for this emblematic French opera, one of the most beloved in the repertoire.Werther, a soul consumed by poetry and longing, falls deeply in love with Charlotte — though she’s already promised to another. Unable to silence his feelings, trapped in a world where social duty outweighs personal truth, he spirals into an all-encompassing melancholy. In this refined bourgeois universe, where emotions are neatly tucked away, an impossible love story unfolds — tender as a memory, sharp as a final goodbye. | ["French, subtitled in French and English"] | ["Werther: Julien Dran","Charlotte: Julie Boulianne","Sophie: Sophie Naubert","Albert: Hugo Laporte ","Le Bailli: Tomislav Lavoie","Schmidt: Jeremy Scinocca","Johann: Dante Mullin Santone","Musical Direction: Jacques Lacombe","Stage Direction: Alain Gauthier","Scenography: Olivier Landreville","Lighting Design: Michael Kangas","Costumes: Leïlah Dufour Forget","Production \/ Presentation: Opéra de Montréal","Co-production: Canadian Opera Company, Vancouver Opera"]

hits.content: Pianist, composer, and conductor Marianne Trudel premieres a bold new work for the Orchestre national de jazz de Montréal (ONJ)—Au centre, la lumière—where orchestral power meets emotional depth. | Known for her fearless blending of improvisation, rich harmonies, and complex structures, Trudel brings both ambition and intimacy to the orchestral format. The program also revisits Dans la Forêt de ma Mémoire (2015), the first work the ONJ entrusted to her—offering a rare look at an artistic voice in full evolution. Poised between tradition and the avant-garde, this concert is one of the defining events of the 2025–2026 musical season. | ["1h20 without intermission"] | [": Marianne Trudel, Au Centre, la Lumière… Marianne Trudel, Dans la Forêt de ma Mémoire","Pianist and conductor: Marianne Trudel","Orchestra: Orchestre national de jazz de Montréal","Production \/ Presentation: Production ONJ"]
